subject: Private deployment: keystore demarcation and regional dataflow annotation
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marta Silva <marta.silva@medsyn.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Private deployment: keystore demarcation and regional dataflow annotation

Hi Marta / team,

Thanks for the call this morning. As promised I'm attaching a working annex that annotates the private-deployment dataflow diagram and proposes a concise keystore demarcation for VPC and on-prem customers. Two things we need to confirm before we send an official DPA addendum:

- Custody split: customer CMK (BYOK) for model input/output and tenant data; Redwood-managed keys only for platform telemetry and runtime health metrics (which we recommend storing in a separate partition).
- Operator access: short, auditable windows for break-glass with live session recordings and immutable audit logs. We propose a 30-minute approval window for urgent recovery ops and a 14-day retention for break-glass justification records.

Ask: can you review the attached `priv-deploy-annex-draft-v2.pdf` and highlight any mandatory regulatory constraints that would require us to change the custody split (e.g., local-key escrow rules or prescriptive export restrictions)? Also confirm whether the telemetry scope (agent heartbeats + anonymized performance counters) is acceptable to Medsyn.

I'll loop Legal on our side (Irene) and Priyom for subprocessor coordination. If this looks okay at a high level, Kimberly will prepare the procurement path.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: priv-deploy-annex-draft-v2.pdf (PDF, 215KB)
From: Marta Silva <marta.silva@medsyn.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Jules Martin <jules.martin@acmehealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 13:47:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Private deployment: keystore demarcation and regional dataflow annotation

Dylan,

Thanks — review underway. A few quick flags from Medsyn compliance:

1) SCCs + Data Transfers: because some processing nodes will originate in the EU and the support/ops team sits in the US, we need explicit mention of transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent) in the annex.
2) Escrow: we cannot agree to any custody model that implies Redwood can unilaterally request custodian key material from a third party. If you propose escrow, it must be customer-controlled with notarized release conditions.
3) Telemetry: acceptable only if pseudonymized at source and cannot be correlated to customer IDs; examples would be aggregate token counts, GPU utilization buckets, and anonymized error codes.

I'll add inline comments to the PDF and upload them tomorrow. Also, can you confirm whether operator sessions are accessible to Redwood engineers by default or only via the break-glass process? That will be a blocker for our security board.

Regards,
Marta Silva
Head of Compliance, Medsyn Therapeutics

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: keystore demarcation and regional dataflow annotation

Dylan / team,

Thanks for the draft — I put a tracked-change summary into the attached PDF and propose the following additions to the annex language (high level):

- Transfers: add a short paragraph committing to SCCs (or EU adequacy mechanism at time of signature) and an obligation to notify within 30 days if a transfer arrangement changes.
- Escrow/Keystore: allow customer-directed escrow releases only upon jointly-signed court order or notarized release plus a two-party approver (customer security officer + Redwood legal) — we will not hold unilateral release keys.
- Operator access: require pre-approval via customer SSO group for all non-emergency sessions. Emergency (break-glass) requires: 1) documented justification in the ticket, 2) an emergency approver e-mail that is preserved in the audit record, 3) session recording + immutable log entry, 4) automated alert to customer security inbox within 1 hour.
- Telemetry: redact any identifier that could be mapped to a tenant id and restrict retention to 90 days by default unless customer requests longer.

I've attached `priv-deploy-annex-draft-v2.pdf` with inline comments and a short summary. We should also create a short one-page matrix that maps what stays on customer keys vs Redwood-managed keys at each network boundary; that will speed the security board review for Medsyn.

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Attachment: priv-deploy-annex-draft-v2.pdf (annotated, 248KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 15:21:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private deployment: keystore demarcation and regional dataflow annotation

Irene / Dylan — adding ops perspective and subprocessor note.

- Subprocessors: I reviewed the current instrumented subprocessors and removed two back-end analytics vendors from the proposed whitelist for private deployments. See attached CSV `subprocessor_revlist_2027-10-19.csv` for the proposed list. For private deployments the subproc footprint is smaller: logging aggregator (customer-owned endpoint), metrics collector (minimal), and platform patch-management partner (only for vulnerability updates under strict access windows).
- Ephemeral telemetry: recommend one-way telemetry flows only; no log rehydration into customer environments. All telemetry forwarded to our SOC must be pseudonymized and stored in a dedicated partition with strict ACLs.
- Procurement ask: Kimberly — are we able to accept a customer-requested 14-day discovery hold for audit evidence versus the standard 90 days? Medsyn may request a shorter window for certain regulated datasets.

I'll update the annex to include a subprocessor change-notice clause (15-day notice for minor changes, 30-day for new subprocessors with access).

Priyom Das
Director, Platform Ops | Redwood Inference
